verses.text: James, a servant of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered among the nations: Greetings.
My brothers and sisters, when all kinds of trials come your way, consider it a joy,
because you know that when your faith is tested, it develops endurance.
Let endurance finish its work so you can be mature and complete, lacking nothing.
If any of you lacks wisdom, ask God, who gives generously to everyone without criticizing, and it will be given to you.
But ask in faith without doubting, because the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, pushed and tossed by the wind.
That person shouldn’t expect to receive anything from the Lord.
They’re divided inside and unstable in everything they do.
Believers in humble circumstances should take pride in their high position.
But the rich should take pride in being brought low, because they’ll pass away like a wildflower.
The sun rises with scorching heat and dries up the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is gone. In the same way, the rich will fade away while going about their business.
Blessed is the person who endures testing, because after standing firm, they’ll receive the crown of life that the Lord promised to those who love him.
No one being tempted should say, “God is tempting me.” God isn’t tempted by evil, and he doesn’t tempt anyone.
Each person is tempted when they’re dragged away and trapped by their own desires.
Then desire gets pregnant and gives birth to sin; and when sin grows up, it gives birth to death.
Don’t be fooled, my dear brothers and sisters.
Every good and perfect gift comes from above, from the Father of lights, who doesn’t change like shifting shadows.
He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, so we would be a kind of firstfruits of all he created.
Understand this, my dear brothers and sisters: everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to get angry,
because human anger doesn’t produce the righteousness God desires.
So get rid of all moral filth and the evil that’s so common, and humbly welcome the word planted in you, which can save you.
Don’t just listen to the word and fool yourselves. Do what it says.
Anyone who listens to the word but doesn’t do it is like someone who looks at their face in a mirror
and, after looking, walks away and immediately forgets what they look like.
But the person who looks closely into the perfect law that gives freedom and keeps at it—not forgetting what they heard, but doing it—will be blessed in what they do.
If someone thinks they’re religious but can’t control their tongue, they’re fooling themselves, and their religion is worthless.
Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is this: care for orphans and widows in their trouble and keep yourself from being polluted by the world.
My brothers and sisters, as you believe in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, don’t show favoritism.
Suppose someone enters your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor person in shabby clothes comes in too.
If you give special attention to the person in fine clothes and say, “Here, have this good seat,” but tell the poor person, “Stand over there,” or “Sit on the floor by my feet,”
haven’t you made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my dear brothers and sisters: didn’t God choose those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
But you’ve dishonored the poor. Aren’t the rich the ones who oppress you and drag you into court?
Don’t they insult the honorable name you bear?
If you really fulfill the royal law found in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you’re doing well.
But if you show favoritism, you’re sinning and the law convicts you as lawbreakers.
Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point is guilty of breaking all of it.
For the one who said, “Don’t commit adultery,” also said, “Don’t murder.” If you don’t commit adultery but do murder, you’ve become a lawbreaker.
Speak and act as people who will be judged by the law that gives freedom.
Judgment without mercy will come to anyone who hasn’t shown mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
My brothers and sisters, what good is it if someone claims to have faith but doesn’t act on it? Can that kind of faith save them?
Suppose a brother or sister has no clothes and no food for the day.
If one of you says, “Go in peace; stay warm and eat well,” but doesn’t give what their body needs, what good is that?
In the same way, faith by itself, if it doesn’t lead to action, is dead.
Someone might say, “You have faith and I have actions.” Show me your faith without actions, and I’ll show you my faith by what I do.
You believe there’s one God. Good! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.
You foolish person, do you need proof that faith without actions is useless?
Wasn’t Abraham our father shown to be righteous by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
You see that faith was working together with his actions, and his faith was made complete by what he did.
That fulfilled the Scripture that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called God’s friend.
You see, a person is shown to be righteous by actions and not by faith alone.
In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute shown to be righteous by what she did when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out another way?
Just as a body without the spirit is dead, so faith without actions is dead.
My brothers and sisters, not many of you should become teachers, because you know teachers will be judged more strictly.
We all stumble in many ways. If someone never slips up in what they say, they’re mature and can control their whole body too.
We put bits in horses’ mouths to make them obey us, and we can guide their whole bodies.
Look at ships too: though they’re large and driven by strong winds, a small rudder steers them wherever the pilot wants.
In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes big claims. A small spark can set a huge forest on fire.
The tongue is a fire, a whole world of evil among our body parts. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures have been tamed by humans,
but no one can tame the tongue. It’s restless and evil, full of deadly poison.
With our tongue we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we curse people made in God’s likeness.
Praise and cursing come from the same mouth. My brothers and sisters, this shouldn’t happen.
Can fresh water and bitter water flow from the same spring?
My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree produce olives, or a grapevine figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let them show it by their good life and deeds done with humility that comes from wisdom.
But if you have bitter envy and selfish ambition in your hearts, don’t brag about it or deny the truth.
That kind of wisdom doesn’t come from above; it’s earthly, unspiritual, and demonic.
Where envy and selfish ambition exist, there’s disorder and every kind of evil practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peace-loving, considerate, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere.
Peacemakers who sow peace harvest righteousness.
What causes fights and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from your desires battling inside you?
You want something but don’t get it, so you kill. You covet but can’t obtain what you want, so you fight and quarrel. You don’t have because you don’t ask God.
When you do ask, you don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives—to spend it on your pleasures.
You unfaithful people! Don’t you know that friendship with the world means hostility toward God? So whoever wants to be a friend of the world makes themselves God’s enemy.
Or do you think Scripture says for no reason that God jealously longs for the spirit he made to live in us?
But he gives more grace. That’s why Scripture says: “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
So submit to God. Resist the devil, and he’ll run away from you.
Come near to God, and he’ll come near to you. Clean your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you divided people.
Grieve, mourn, and cry. Let your laughter turn to mourning and your joy to gloom.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he’ll lift you up.

Brothers and sisters, don’t speak against one another. Anyone who speaks against a brother or sister, or judges them, speaks against the law and judges it. If you judge the law, you aren’t following it—you’re judging it.
There’s only one Lawgiver and Judge, the one who can save and destroy. So who are you to judge your neighbor?
Now listen, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we’ll go to this or that city, spend a year there, do business, and make money.”
You don’t even know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? You’re a mist that appears for a little while and then disappears.
Instead, you should say, “If the Lord wills, we’ll live and do this or that.”
As it is, you brag in your arrogant plans. All such boasting is evil.
So if you know the good you should do and don’t do it, that’s sin.
Now listen, you rich people: cry and wail over the misery coming your way.
Your wealth has rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes.
Your gold and silver are corroded, and their corrosion will testify against you and eat your flesh like fire. You’ve piled up treasure in the last days.
Look! The wages you failed to pay the workers who harvested your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
You’ve lived in luxury and self-indulgence on earth. You’ve fattened yourselves for the day of slaughter.
You’ve condemned and murdered the righteous person, who wasn’t opposing you.
So be patient, brothers and sisters, until the Lord comes. See how the farmer waits for the valuable harvest from the land, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.
You too should be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.
Brothers and sisters, don’t complain about one another, or you’ll be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!
Brothers and sisters, take the prophets who spoke in the Lord’s name as examples of suffering and patience.
We call those who endured blessed. You’ve heard about Job’s endurance and seen what the Lord finally did, because the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
Above all, my brothers and sisters, don’t swear—not by heaven or earth or anything else. Let your “Yes” mean yes and your “No” mean no, so you won’t fall under judgment.
Is anyone among you suffering? Let them pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let them sing praise.
Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the church’s elders to pray over them and anoint them with oil in the Lord’s name.
The prayer offered in faith will make the sick person well; the Lord will raise them up. If they’ve sinned, they’ll be forgiven.
So confess your sins to one another and pray for one another so you can be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.
Elijah was a human being just like us. He prayed earnestly that it wouldn’t rain, and it didn’t rain on the land for three and a half years.
Then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain and the land produced its crops.
My brothers and sisters, if one of you wanders from the truth and someone brings them back,
remember this: whoever turns a sinner back from their mistaken path will save them from death and cover many sins.
